# Experimental design — parametric surrogates for DrivAerNet++ aerodynamic drag

## 1. Research question and pre-registered hypotheses

**RQ.** On the DrivAerNet++ 26-parameter design space (fastback, notchback, estateback body styles), does the predictive performance of surrogate models built from the parametric descriptors **improve with training set size** and **differ across model architectures** for aerodynamic drag prediction?

| ID | Hypothesis | Statistical target | Decision cell |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Size main effect — performance improves with n | LMM fixed effect for log10(n) on RMSE (negative) | Adjusted p < 0.01 (per architecture) |
| H2 | Architecture main effect — at a fixed n, architectures differ | Layer-1 omnibus (Friedman across 6 architectures) + at least one Holm-adjusted pairwise Layer-1 hit | at size k = K (largest): omnibus p < 0.05 |
| H3 | Size × architecture interaction — curves have different shapes | LMM interaction architecture × log10(n); Layer-2 Holm-adjusted test on per-architecture power-law exponent c | LMM Wald p < 0.01; ≥ 1 Holm-adjusted Layer-2 pair |
| H4 | LOSO robustness — pooled-vs-LOSO ranking does not invert | Spearman ρ between pooled and LOSO mean RMSE rankings; maximum rank shift per architecture | Spearman ρ ≥ 0.6 and rank shift ≤ 2 slots |

## 2. Dataset and parameterisation of unknowns

The dataset file is not present in the workspace; the design therefore proceeds symbolically and binds every dataset-dependent value to a named design parameter `Pn` with an "unspecified at design time; to be supplied from the dataset card" default that enters at a fixed workflow entry point.

| ID | Parameter | Workflow entry point (section §) | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | N_fastback, N_notchback, N_estateback, total N | §4 (schedule), §5 (folds) | unspecified at design time |
| P2 | Whether the 26 parameters are identical across body styles or partly variant-specific | §3 (preprocessor), §8 (feature-leakage check) | assume **shared**; flag sensitivity toggle if variant-specific |
| P3 | Units & scaling of the 26 parameters (lengths, ratios, zero-bounded quantities) | §3 (preprocessor) | unspecified at design time; applied as StandardScaler with optional log1p on declared zero-bounded fields |
| P4 | Whether DrivAerNet++ publishes a canonical train/test split | §5 (partitioning) | use canonical split if present; otherwise build a seed-derived stratified split and disclose the seed |
| P5 | Target variable: Cd / F_d / Cd_p and reference conditions (ρ, U, A) | §6 (metrics & units) | **Cd, dimensionless**; tagged so swapping to F_d (N) or Cd_p only changes the units row and the nRMSE reference |
| P6 | Mutually exclusive body-style labels or multi-label | §5 (LOSO, stratification) | assume **mutually exclusive**; sensitivity toggle documented if multi-label |
| P7 | Master seed for splits, subsampling, MLP init, GP optimizer | §8 (controls) | seed value to be fixed at design time (placeholder: 0) |
| P8 | Pilot budget for pre-registering hyperparameters (M1–M6) | §3, §10 | to be fixed at design time (upper bound: ≤ 10 % of N_train or ≤ 300 designs, whichever smaller) |

## 3. Surrogate model set and pre-registered configurations

Six architectures are compared. **Hyperparameters are fixed per architecture across all training sizes**; their final values are locked by a pre-registration pilot (P8) before any size-grid fit is opened. The fixed-configuration policy is a deliberate confound with the learning-curve interpretation: the curve measures "this pre-registered configuration of family X" rather than "the best achievable instance of family X at each size".

| ID | Model | Library & class skeleton | Pre-registered hyperparameters (locked by pilot P8) | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | Linear OLS baseline | `sklearn.linear_model.LinearRegression` | none | point |
| M2 | Degree-2 polynomial + ridge | `preprocessing.PolynomialFeatures(degree=2, interaction_only=False, include_bias=False)` → `linear_model.Ridge(alpha=α_ridge)` | α_ridge (TBD by pilot) | point |
| M3 | Anisotropic-ARD-RBF Gaussian Process | `gaussian_process.GaussianProcessRegressor(kernel=RBF(length_scale=np.ones(26), length_scale_bounds=(1e-3, 1e3)) * ConstantKernel, alpha=α_noise, normalize_y=True, n_restarts_optimizer=3)` | α_noise, kernel priors (TBD by pilot) | point + 95 % PI |
| M4 | Random Forest | `ensemble.RandomForestRegressor(criterion="squared_error", n_estimators=N_trees, max_features="sqrt", min_samples_leaf=msl, n_jobs=1, random_state=seed)` | N_trees, msl (TBD by pilot) | point |
| M5 | Gradient Boosting | `ensemble.HistGradientBoostingRegressor(loss="squared_error", max_iter=N_iter, learning_rate=lr, max_leaf_nodes=mln, l2_regularization=l2, random_state=seed)` | N_iter, lr, max_leaf_nodes, l2 (TBD by pilot) | point |
| M6 | MLP, 2 hidden layers 128 → 64, ReLU, early stopping | `torch.nn.Sequential(Linear(26,128), ReLU(), Linear(128,64), ReLU(), Linear(64,1))`; Adam; MSE loss | lr, batch, max_epochs, early-stopping patience (TBD by pilot) | point |

Pilot procedure (§10): on a stratified sub-sample of N_train at size upper-bounded by P8, run a bounded broad search (grid for tree/MLP HPs; optimizer-restart sweep for α_noise / length-scale priors for M3), record metric, lock the configuration. The pilot does **not** participate in the per-size grid.

## 4. Training-size schedule and resampling

**Schedule.** Geometric, K = 6 spacing exponents, ≈ 7 sizes including the full training pool:

> n_k = floor(N_train · 2^k / 2^K), k = 0, 1, ..., K

Identifiability floor for M2 (degree-2 polynomial over 26 features → 351 unknowns under StandardScaler + interaction expansion): n_0 ≥ N_poly minimum. When P1 implies n_0 < N_poly, drop the smallest k values until n_min ≥ N_poly. N_poly itself is a parameter (default 150); it must be ≥ ~100–200 in practice. The exact threshold is set at design time, not invented.

**Resampling.** K_repl = 10 seeded replicates per (architecture, size) cell. All M1–M6 architectures observe the **same K_repl training subsets** at every size k, so all per-cell comparisons are paired. Per-replicate PRNG is derived deterministically from master seed P7 plus a per-replicate offset.

**Held-out test set.** A single stratified-proportional holdout carved out from the dataset once (using P4 if a canonical test partition exists; otherwise a seed-controlled fallback). The same held-out set is used by every (architecture, size, replicate) cell of the primary analysis, so test statistics are paired across the full grid.

## 5. Body-style partitioning

### 5.1 Primary — pooled, stratified-proportional

- Carve the held-out test set once via stratified proportional sampling on body style from the full dataset (uses P4 if canonical; otherwise build with P7).
- N_train = remaining designs. For each replicate r and size k, draw n_k stratified proportional on body style from N_train.

### 5.2 Secondary — leave-one-style-out (LOSO), 3 × 6 matrix

- For s ∈ {fastback, notchback, estateback}: training pool = N_train ∩ ¬s; test pool = all designs with style s.
- Same K_repl replicates reused; replicates share the LOSO partitions (the LOSO test fold is a deterministic function of style labels).
- Cells: 3 held-out styles × 6 architectures = 18 LOSO cells.
- **Leakage guard:** no observation with style s appears in any LOSO training fold when s is the held-out style (§8).
- Mutually-exclusivity (P6) is the working assumption; if the dataset is multi-label, swap the partition for an "any-overlap" rule with explicit excluded-overlap zone and re-issue the LOSO matrix.

The LOSO analysis is paired with the pooled curve: 6 architectures compared on both, with the architecture-on-LOSO ordering shown alongside the pooled ordering (H4).

## 6. Evaluation metrics with units

All metrics computed on the held-out test set. Units are tagged on P5; swapping target changes only this section.

| Metric | Definition | Units | Reported for |
|---|---|---|---|
| R² | 1 − SS_res / SS_tot | dimensionless | M1..M6 |
| RMSE | sqrt(mean((y − ŷ)²)) | declared target units (P5) | M1..M6 |
| MAE | mean(abs(y − ŷ)) | declared target units (P5) | M1..M6 |
| nRMSE | RMSE / std(y_test) | dimensionless | M1..M6 |
| 95 % PI empirical coverage | mean(I{y_low ≤ y ≤ y_up}) with y_low = μ − 1.96 σ, y_up = μ + 1.96 σ | dimensionless | **M3 only** |
| Mean 95 % PI width | mean(y_up − y_low) | declared target units (P5) | **M3 only** |

Coverage and width are not reported for deterministic models — they would not be meaningful.

## 7. Statistical comparison plan

### 7.1 Layer 1 — per-size vertical separation (paired Wilcoxon)

- Within each size k, for each unordered pair of architectures (p, q) ∈ pairs(M1..M6): paired Wilcoxon signed-rank on the K_repl = 10 RMSE samples.
- 15 pairs × 7 sizes = up to 105 raw Layer-1 p-values.
- **Holm-Bonferroni correction is applied separately within each size** (across the 15 pairs at that size), preserving power at small k where fewer pairs are likely to reject.
- Report Δ_{pq,k} = median(RMSE_q − RMSE_p) per pair per size, alongside the adjusted p.
- Optional guard: per-size Friedman omnibus across 6 architectures; reject H2 only if at least one adjusted pairwise Layer-1 comparison is significant at k = K.

### 7.2 Layer 2 — curve-level shape (per-architecture power-law fit + paired test)

- Within each replicate r (1..K_repl), for each architecture m, fit
  > RMSE_m,k,r = a_m,r + b_m,r · n_k^(−c_m,r),  k = 0..K
  with a ≥ 0, b ≥ 0, c ∈ (0, 2]. Use `scipy.optimize.curve_fit` starting from a log-linear OLS fit on (log n_k, log max(RMSE − min_RMSE, ε)).
- For each unordered pair of architectures (p, q): paired Wilcoxon on {c_p,r} vs {c_q,r} across the K_repl = 10 replicates.
- 15 pairs total; **Holm-Bonferroni correction across the 15 pairs.**
- Also report Δ_a and Δ_b for the asymptotic and bulk contributions.

### 7.3 Mandatory robustness companion — Linear Mixed Model

- Model: `metric ~ C(architecture) * log10(n) + (1 | replicate)`
- Random effect: replicate (intercepts).
- Fixed effects: architecture (six levels), log10(n), interaction.
- Test for H3: Type-III Wald on the interaction term "slope differs across architectures".
- Diagnostics: residual heteroscedasticity across n; if detected, fall back to a log-transformed target within the LMM but keep the per-size Layer-1 reporting on the original (declared) units.
- The LMM is a single conditional test (Wald, df = 5 for the interaction); no further correction is applied to it.

### 7.4 Multiplicity & power notes

- Layer-1 Holm is **per size** — small-k corrections may reject few pairs; that is accepted.
- Layer-2 Holm is across the 15 architecture pairs.
- LMM interaction p is one conditional test and does not enter either Holm family.
- No cross-layer correction — each layer answers a different pre-registered question.

## 8. Controls and leakage prevention

| ID | Control | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Master seed P7 fixed; per-replicate PRNG derived deterministically (P7 + r-offset) | `numpy.random.default_rng(P7 + r); `torch.manual_seed`/`torch.cuda.manual_seed_all` set in M6 only |
| C2 | Identical preprocessor across architectures, fit on per-replicate training **only** | `sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler` fit on the K_repl × n_k training subset; the same scaler instance type (not state) is reused across M1..M6 |
| C3 | MLP early-stopping calibration fold drawn from per-replicate training pool, consistent across sizes | 80 / 20 split of per-replicate training subset, replicated at every k so the calibration subset is identical across sizes within a replicate |
| C4 | LOSO leakage guard | Assert that no observation with held-out style s appears in any LOSO training fold when s is the held-out style; assert the count |
| C5 | Feature-leakage check | Input matrix must have exactly 26 columns matching P2; raise on schema drift; strip ID and constant columns; log the parameter list used |
| C6 | Style-proportional sanity | Per replicate, body-style proportions in the train subsample must lie within ε (default 0.05) of the stratified test proportions |
| C7 | Reproducibility manifest | Per-replicate JSON: seeds, HP configs, scaler statistics, library versions, sample counts |

## 9. Feasibility and runtime budget

**Environment.** 24 CPU cores, no GPU, no network, system Python 3.12.3. ML libraries (scikit-learn ≥ 1.4; xgboost ≥ 2.0 optional; torch ≥ 2.2 optional) are **not preinstalled**. Installing them is an external dependency outside the design contract; the design assumes they are available at execution time and falls back to sklearn-only if not.

**Computational shape (order-of-magnitude only).**

- Primary pooled analysis: K_arch × K_sizes × K_repl = 6 × 7 × 10 ≈ 420 fits on the largest size is the worst case; GP typically dominates.
- LOSO: K_arch × K_styles × K_repl = 6 × 3 × 10 = 180 fits, computed on the LOSO training pools.
- Pilot: ≤ P8 designs × 6 architectures.
- Total ≈ 600 + pilot fits.

**Cost drivers (rough ranking, no numeric claims).**

| Architecture | Dominant cost component | Fit-level rough category |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Linear OLS | closed-form | negligible |
| M2 Degree-2 + Ridge | 351-feature closed-form | negligible |
| M3 GP ARD RBF | n³ kernel inversion + hyper-restarts | dominant cost on large k (parameterized at execution time) |
| M4 RF | 500 trees, embarassingly parallel across cores | modest |
| M5 GBM | 500 boosting iterations, histogram splits | modest |
| M6 MLP | epochs × mini-batches × 26 input / 192 hidden units | modest (CPU-bound; no GPU available) |

**Parallelisation policy.**

- Parallelise **across replicates**, not across sizes within an architecture. Replicates are independent and seed-isolated; sizes within a replicate share calibration fold offsets and must run serially to keep seeds deterministic.
- Use up to 10 of 24 cores for the primary pooled grid (`joblib.Parallel(n_jobs=10)`-style batching).
- LOSO fits reuse the same parallel regime on the LOSO training pools.
